name: The Campaign for North Africa (campaign game)
notes: The full campaign: forces, supplies and construction are set up as in Graziani's Offensive (60.0), and the Initiative follows that scenario's restriction, after which it is found normally (64.4).
Normal game actions are all allowed, including Raids on Rommel and the Commonwealth Fleet (64.51).
Axis Malta Air Availability comes from the campaign-game row of the Axis Strategic Airforce Commitment Chart (64.52).
Abstracted play: use the abstraction rules of 32.0, 47.0 and 58.0 together with the abstracted set-up of the starting scenario group and the replacement adjustments of 64.5 (64.6).

levels.supply: Every hex held for one full Game-Turn, by units that trace a convoy route of no more than 90 truck Movement Points to a Supply Dump that is itself supplied in any way from Tobruk or Tripoli. Wins at once, whatever the turn (64.71).

notes: The Axis automatic victory (64.71) is shown as a strategic level; the rules call it simply winning the game.

Commonwealth automatic victory (64.72): from OpStage 1 of Game-Turn 35 on, if no Axis combat unit on the map can trace supply of at most 60 truck Movement Points to a Supply Dump and on to Tobruk or Tripoli, the Commonwealth wins at once. Air and coastal shipping units do not count.
Occupation points (64.73): a place scores only for a combat unit that meets the end-of-game supply test in rules/scenarios/50-campaign-game.md#victory.
Replacement points (64.74): each side scores one point per Replacement Point allotted on its Production Charts and never used. Aircraft and trucks do not count, nor, for the Commonwealth, infantry.

Victory level (64.76) is set by the ratio of the larger total to the smaller: equal totals draw; above 1:1 up to 1.5:1 is a Marginal Victory; above 1.5:1 up to 2.5:1 a Decisive Victory; above 2.5:1 a Smashing Victory. These are ratios, not point margins, so 'margins' is not used.
